[CONTRIBUTION EVENT]
- Type: Time (Minutes)
- Amount: 30
- Description: Responding to Win on his document
  
  @钟致颖WIN  just got back from the rainforest
  
  I finished looking at the document you shared. Some logistics related question I have in mind after reading through your document, basically a decision tree to be navigated.
  
  
  - what do you think is the most appropriate product form to be distributed via your distribution network?
  
  - In what form do you expect the products to be in when you receive it to the portion of the (manufacturing) supply chain you are managing in China
  
      - already converted to its final form before receiving them into your distribution network or 
      - you have facilities to convert the cacao beans or
      - you have facilities to complete the final assembly of the already processed cacao beans?
  
  - which is the port of entry you have in mind for receiving the desired form for the product? 
  
  - What is the amount you have in mind for pilot testing?
  
      - if in terms of cacao beans: kilograms targeted
      - if in finished or partially assembled SKU: Amount of units
  
  
  My sense is the size for the pilot you are referring to will most likely fall under AirFreight instead of Sea Freight. 
  
      - Sea Freight you are looking at 12.5 tons, we are already past the peak cacao harvesting and processing season this year to pack cacao beans into full containers (orders need to have been placed during May 2026)
  
      - For airfreight, you are looking at maximum weight below 1,000 kilograms per payload
  
  
  Caveats
  
  - If end product you plan to receive into your distribution network is finished product or partially converted product but not yet fully assembled, 
  
      - then the cacao beans will need to be air freight from the Amazon rainforest state of Para to our factory facility in Bahia to be converted before being airfreight out to your destination port. I am assuming Shen Zhen China or Hong Kong. Correct me if I am wrong
  
  
  
  - If end product you plant to receive into your distribution network is raw cacao beans, 
  
      - I have informed the cooperative to start their registration proess for MAPA registration number which is the first step before they can start their registration process with the Chinese GACC system.
  
  
  - If end product to be distributed into your distribution network is not cacao beans, and partial manufacturing is expected to be handled in Brazil
  
  	- then we need to know the target production specifications for our manufacturing facility before it gets shipped
  
  
  - If end product to be distributed into your distribution network is not cacao beans, and complete manufacturing is expected to be handled in Brazil
  
  	- then we need to know the target production specifications that our manufacturing facility knows what needs to be produced
  
  	- then the final packaging material needed for the manufacturing process needs to be shipped to the Brazilian side before conversion can happen
